external_entities.name: developers
external_entities.description: People who push branches to the git server and can manually trigger rebuilds of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: Public internet package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the image registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be manually used to rebuild main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: Uses a shared build token to call the deploy controller. Developers can log in and kick off a rebuild of main by hand.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current image SHA for the estate and responds to store server release queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: Small server in each store back office running the till software as a container. It polls the deploy controller, pulls a changed image, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: Git server receiving developer branches and providing source to the build runner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: Registry storing finished container images tagged with commit SHAs and serving images to store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows store server pulls, but what a store server presents to it has not been documented.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developers push branches to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the self-hosted git server after a merge.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source
data_flows.data_description: source code for the merged change

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry while resolving dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.data_description: container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: make current release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: image SHA and requested current release

data_flows.name: ask current release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller once a minute for the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Corporate network containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: Separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: In-store estate containing the store servers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: retail WAN
trust_boundaries.description: WAN used for traffic between stores and the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: Public internet network containing the public package registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The build runner holds or handles credentials because it uses the shared build token to call the deploy controller.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the runner uses a shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller holds business-critical data because it holds the estate's current release image SHA.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the deploy controller holds the record of which image SHA the estate should be on.

assumptions.assumption: The store server supports availability-critical operations because it runs the till software in each store.
assumptions.basis: The text states that each store has a server running the till software and describes the store estate deployment path.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry supports availability-critical operations because store servers pull their running image from it.
assumptions.basis: The text states that store servers pull the image from the registry and restart the container when the release changes.

assumptions.assumption: The build-controller flow carries credentials because the runner authenticates with a shared build token.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the token the runner uses to call the controller is a shared build token.
